Beating the Booking Giants: A Survival Guide for Travel Agents

Facebook
X
Pinterest
WhatsApp
Linkedin
Email
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 7:00
    Instaread

    As a travel agency operator, you probably know the feeling when a client asks, “Can you match this price on Booking.com?” It’s an awkward question, but it’s also a reality of the industry. 

    Online travel agencies (OTAs) like Expedia and Booking.com have huge advertising budgets and have made booking travel incredibly convenient. In fact, according to market reports, these two giants together control roughly 65% of the global OTA market.

    Clearly, competing on price is a non-option for independent agencies. But price was never really the game. Your advantage is what happens beyond the booking screen: your ability to offer something OTAs can’t offer. That’s what we’ll be talking about in this guide.

    Provide What OTAs Can’t Offer

    Your flexibility is your first advantage as an independent travel agency.

    Think about it. When a flight gets canceled at 2 AM, who’s the client going to call for a quick resolution? A chatbot? A 1-800 number with a 45-minute hold? As an independent travel agency, you can be there to deal with client issues day or night. That human connection, which most OTAs can’t offer, is gold.

    And it’s not just about fixing issues. You can create tailored itineraries that go far beyond a simple flight and hotel bundle. Plus, you’ve likely got local connections and can offer exclusive packages they can’t find online.

    Otto de Vries, CEO of ASATA, puts it perfectly when speaking to Southern Africa’s Travel News: “OTAs often fall short when it comes to providing the nuanced, personalized service that many travelers seek. This is where travel agents and advisers continue to shine, offering tailored expertise and support that automated systems simply can’t match.”

    Use PPC Advertising to Capture High-Intent Travelers

    Instead of trying to outspend the big OTAs on generic terms like “cheap flight,” use PPC to reach people who actually want what you sell.

    Think about intent. Someone Googling “flights to London” may still be browsing. But someone typing “honeymoon weekend in Little Venice” has a much more specific need and may be looking for help planning the trip. Long-tail keywords like this, according to a review by Electronic Commerce Research on Springer Nature, can help advertisers capture niche markets.

    This is where PPC can be a big help. You can use it to target those specific, high-intent keywords that your agency is uniquely qualified to answer. If you cannot manage these details in-house, partner with the best travel PPC agency you can find. 

    The goal, as Teckgeekz puts it, is to target users right when they’re searching with high intent. Only the right PPC partner can help you achieve this.

    Strengthen Your Digital Presence Beyond Ads

    While PPC brings people in, you need a solid foundation to turn those visitors into clients. This means getting serious about SEO. We’ve already talked about long-tail keywords in the context of PPC, but they can be just as useful for organic search.

    Just as important are your reviews. Studies show that up to 96% of customers check reviews before doing business with a brand. That’s how important reviews can be. They’re your social proof, helping build the same kind of trust that OTA ratings provide.

    And don’t forget email marketing. Sending a quick “thinking of you” email with a deal on a destination they love, or simply reminding them to book before prices go up, keeps you top of mind.

    Offer Value-Added Services

    Remember the 2 AM phone call we talked about earlier in this piece? That’s one way independent travel agencies are better than OTAs. But the real value-added services make that 2 AM call almost unnecessary. 

    Value-added services give clients even more reasons to book through you.

    For example, guide them through travel insurance. A recent survey showed that 63% of Americans skipped it entirely on their 2025 trips, often without realizing the risk they were taking. You can also help clients with visa paperwork,  recover funds for canceled or unused tickets, lost passports or travel issues abroad, and lots more.

    Finally, add a simple loyalty or referral program, and you’ve turned a one-time booking into an ongoing relationship.

    Many OTAs can’t offer services like these simply because they’re too big or very far from their clients.

    Use Technology to Improve the Customer Experience

    Finally, use technology to make your service easier to buy. Websites. Social media. DMs. Make it easy for people to contact you and manage their bookings through these channels. 

    More importantly, invest in a CRM. It’s the backbone of a modern agency and lets you track client preferences. You don’t want to be re-interviewing them every time they call or suggesting experiences they’ve already had. And automate the mundane stuff. Install an AI chatbot on your website that can handle basic customer enquiries, leaving you with more time for the important conversations.

    The truth is that the travel industry is already moving in this direction. Just booking automation for the travel agency market alone is expected to hit $12.3 billion by 2033. You don’t want to be left behind.

    FAQs

    Can a small travel agency really compete with big OTA ad budgets?

    Absolutely. You don’t need a massive budget. You need a smart one. By targeting high-intent, niche keywords, a well-run PPC campaign can outperform generic OTA ads on conversion rate. It’s about attracting the right customer, not the most customers.

    What’s the biggest advantage a travel agency has over OTAs?

    It will always be a personalized service. Your hands-on approach, as well as your ability to support clients before, during, and after their trip, is something OTAs simply can’t offer. You give peace of mind, not just a booking confirmation.

    Is PPC worth it for a small travel agency?

    Totally. The trick is to target specific experiences like “family safari in South Africa.” Then use retargeting for those who visit your site but don’t book. This keeps your costs controlled while catching those warm leads.

    Final Words

    Online travel agencies and booking giants are here to stay. There’s no denying that. But independent, and even small travel agencies like yours, aren’t going anywhere, either. While you may not be able to out-discount or outspend them, you can definitely out-serve and out-target them. Hopefully, this guide has shown you how to do that successfully.
